description.value: The present study used functional magnetic resonance imaging to compare brain activity in smokers treated with the nicotine conjugate vaccine NicVAX with that in non-treated smokers during smoking cue exposure and a working memory task.

spans.text: The present study made use of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to compare brain activity in smokers treated with the nicotine conjugate vaccine NicVAX with that in non-treated smokers when both were exposed to smoking cues and a working memory task.

description.value: Participants were assigned randomly to receive five subsequent injections with either the NicVAX vaccine or a placebo, and were tested on two occasions with nicotine gum or regular chewing gum.

spans.text: Participants were assigned randomly to receive five subsequent injections with either 400 μg/ml of the 3′-aminomethylnicotine Pseudomonas aeruginosa r-Exoprotein conjugate vaccine (NicVAX; Nabi Biopharmaceuticals, Rockville, MD, USA) ( n = 28) or a placebo ( n = 20).
Challenge order was single-blind and randomized.
